original_question: In the quantum-gravitational treatment of black holes, should one impose a time-symmetric Weyl-tensor condition on all spacelike singularities, and would doing so eliminate genuine black-hole interiors, horizons, or information loss? Because the black-hole interior is causally inaccessible and quantum gravity no longer sharply distinguishes past from future singularities, the unresolved issue is whether a symmetric singularity condition is the correct way to understand black-hole entropy and avoid the information-loss paradox.
